reason: Sage parity only: Sage taxes its 'Temporary/Part time' status at a flat 25% (R1 125.00). The calculator has no tax-status input and applies the tables (R0.00), which is the statutory figure if the employee is in standard employment (22+ hours a week). G21 Rev 1 p. 27-28 decides the treatment from hours and day rate, not from a status label.
closedBy: W3 tax status: hours-per-week and day-rate inputs that classify standard / deemed standard / non-standard employment per G21 p. 27-28. Must NOT be closed by taxing a status label at a flat 25%; if the inputs show standard employment, the fix is to correct this fixture's expectation instead.

reason: Sage excludes an independent contractor from UIF and SDL. Costed with the default employee set-up (UIF and SDL on), the calculator levies R70.00 each. A contractor set up correctly (uifExcluded true, earning not SDL-applicable) matches Sage: see sage-2027-03-rassie-contractor-setup. The gap is that no tax status drives those defaults.
closedBy: W3 tax status: an independent-contractor status that sets the UIF and SDL defaults

reason: An IRP3(b) fixed-percentage directive must be applied as its percentage (G21 Rev 1 p. 15, 17). The calculator only takes a lump-sum directive's PAYE, so it applies the tables: R4 681.00 against R6 000.00.

As fixed-rate-directive-20pct, with a retirement annuity: the directive percentage applies before allowable deductions (G21 Rev 1 p. 15), so PAYE is 20% of R30 000 = R6 000.00; the calculator takes the RA off and applies the tables: R3 901.00.

R4 000 for 160 hours is R25.00 an hour, below the R28.79 national minimum wage (from 1 March 2025), so the employee does not qualify and ETI is nil (SARS ETI page). The calculator has no hours or minimum-wage input and claims R1 500.00.
closedBy: W3 (ETI): hours paid and the minimum-wage condition in the ETI calc, with the 160-hour apportionment
